title: bye, your, friend
parentNote: Three words to remember, and between them they let your child read something this course has never been able to write before: a goodbye. Friend is the hard one. It looks like it ought to be "free-end", because ie has said /eye/ ever since tie and pie, and instead it is said "frend". The thing to hold on to is that the word end is sitting right there inside it — a friend sticks with you to the end. Your comes next, and those last three letters say /or/, not "ow-er". Bye is kind: it is just by with an e stuck on, and the e behaves itself. If your child reads friend as "free-end", don't say no. Say the word back whole, put a finger on the end in it, and carry on. This one takes a dozen sightings rather than a lesson.

activities.prompt: This one is kind to you. It is the word by with an e stuck on the end, and it still says bye.

The e on the end is silent, so it sticks to the v and they go together: w, ay, v, d.

activities.text: Say bye to your father, and then get your boots on.
Is that your bag, or did your friend bring it?
My friend sat down on the step and did not say a thing.
A friend is a thing you can not get in a shop.
It is hard to say bye to a friend, so I did not say it at all.

activities.title: The day Sam went
activities.prompt: This is a story with a bye in it. Some of the words in it are hard to say out loud, and the boy in it can not say them at all at first.
lines: Sam is my friend. He is my best friend, and he is in the house next to us.
Then a big truck came, and men got all the things out of that house and in the truck.
"We go tomorrow," said Sam. "My father got a job a long way off."
I did not want to say bye, so I did not say it at all.
I went in, and I got under my bed, and I did not get out all day.
In the morning the truck is still there, and Sam is on the step with a bag.
"This is for you," he said. "It is your bag now."
It is the red bag with the stars on it. I want that bag so much.
I did not say a thing back. My mouth went stiff and I looked down at the grass.
Then the truck went off down the hill, and I ran after it, and I yelled.
A hand came out of the truck and waved, all the way to the end of the hill.
"Bye is not the end," said my mother. "It is just a thing you say when you go."
Sam will send me a letter, and I will send a letter back. And the red bag is my bag now.
